ladder_hall.name: Ladder Hall
ladder_hall.description: A 5.85 m measuring rack that REPORTS ON four fractal benches and refuses to draw any of them. Four bays stand in one row on one plinth under one datum rail, and each bay holds a stack of plain slats whose HEIGHTS are order statistics read off one of the four benches' own code - fractal_arch_bench, sierpinski_bench, mandelbrot_bench, julia_bench. All four declare the same five-word ladder, character for character, and this hall reuses it verbatim: figure, series, seed, relief, section. What they do NOT share is how many rungs that word buys - 4, 5, 6 and 6 - so the row is deliberately ragged, and the raggedness is a fact about the family rather than a layout error. The second channel switches what a rung is reckoned AGAINST: `mass` is how much of its own field the construction still covers, `count` is how many pieces it is in. Counted by measure all four benches move; counted by parts, the two escape-time benches are FLAT LINES, because 5184 boxes at 4 iterations is 5184 boxes at 70. The two readings disagree about which benches are climbing at all, and about the direction for the arch, which is the only bay where mass rises with the rung.
dev_themes: a shared value list that shares no rung count
counted by parts, half the family is not climbing
the rack that refuses to draw the figure
interactions: read the row left to right at series - four benches' whole climbs laid out in space, 4 / 5 / 6 / 6 rungs, ragged because the family is
switch to count and watch bays C and D go flat: an escape-time test instantiates the same 5184 boxes whatever you ask it
walk to seed in count and find bays C and D UNMOVED from figure while bays A and B collapse - the seed of a formula is not a smaller object
walk to section and watch a lit seam post appear in every bay: the one thing all four benches draw at that value and at no other
ladder_hall.capacity: SEE that a recursive construction makes two separable claims at every rung and that both survive a still - how much of its own field it still COVERS, and how many PIECES it is in - and that the four benches answer them in different directions. Substitution ADDS material as it recurses (the arch rises 0.0975 to 0.4105); removal is multiplication by 3/4 forever; the Mandelbrot falls toward a POSITIVE limit because the set has area; the Julia at c = -0.4+0.6i falls toward ZERO because that c is outside M and the filled set is a dust. SEE ALSO the flatness: counted by parts, the two escape-time bays do not climb at all, and a five-word vocabulary that four codebases spell identically buys 4, 5, 6 and 6 rungs.
ladder_hall.qfep_connection: F is the token: one string out of five, spelled the same in four independently written files and matched character for character by four `match` statements. E is the irreducible difference underneath - a recursion DEPTH decided before any geometry exists on one side of the family, a per-pixel RESULT on the other, so iteration MULTIPLIES elements in two bays and REFINES a raster of constant size in the other two. lambda is what each bench is willing to spend on the word: 2^d - 1 arches, 3^d leaves, 5184 boxes, 5184 boxes. The dark spot is the REFUSAL. This hall does not draw the gasket, the arcade or the escape-time panel, and a viewer cannot verify from the picture that bay B is a removal at all - what is foreclosed is the sight of the four figures, and with it any reading of WHERE in the plane each construction acts. What is bought is the one reading the gauge permits: four construction principles compared at the same pixel scale under one word, which no bench's own room could ever show.
ladder_hall.relationships:
Synthesised out of the four scenes that declare a `ladder` axis, all four registered in commons/artifacts/registry/fractals.json: [[fractal_arch_bench]] (commons/artifacts/fractal_arch_bench/fractal_arch_bench.gd), [[sierpinski_bench]], [[mandelbrot_bench]] and [[julia_bench]]. Verified this pass: those are the only four tokens in the corpus declaring `ladder`, and all four now declare the same five values in the same order.

CONSTRUCTION BORROWED FROM [[pressure_yard]] and, through it, [[tier_terrarium]]: two channels that pin each other so neither can read the other's number. There: spread varied height at a pinned headcount, count varied headcount on a pinned ladder. Here: `ladder` alone fixes how many slats, their LENGTHS, their Z and whether the seam post exists, and `reckoning` alone fixes the slat HEIGHTS. The row form - plinth, pads, kerbs, datum rail, order statistics as slats - is pressure_yard's, at a wider pitch and one rung shorter.

WORD BORROWED FROM [[grain_block]]: `reckoning` is not minted here. grain_block.gd:104 declares `@export_enum("none", "mass", "void", "count") var reckoning: String = "none"`, the corpus's only prior use, and this hall takes two of its four in the source's own order. See dna.kin for why `none` and `void` are refused rather than dropped.

LAW 11 KIN: [[pressure_yard]], [[taxonomy_hall]] and [[selection_garden]] are the corpus's other sparse-not-small subjects. This one's union box is 58.68% of frame WIDTH while its ink swings from 15.1% to 42.3% of the crop, which is a wider swing than any of them.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: THE HEIGHT IS THE CONSTRAINT, NOT THE FOOTPRINT, exactly as for pressure_yard. The plinth is 5.850 x 0.560 m (PLINTH_SIZE, gd:477), six cells by one, but the rack stands 4.440 m from the plinth underside (-0.100) to the top of the datum rail (RAIL_Y 4.290 + RAIL_SIZE.y/2 0.050 = 4.340). That needs FIVE cells of headroom, and a ceiling at 4 decapitates the datum rail - which is the reference every bay is read against and, worse, the thing that holds the framing constant across the ten variants, so losing it costs the exhibit its argument rather than a detail. front 4 because a 5.85 m row wants the reader far enough back to hold four bays at once; back 0 because everything the axes draw faces the approach, the deepest thing in the rack is the seam post at z -0.270, and the whole assembly is 0.56 m deep.

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry - the rack is BoxMesh at named constants (gd:664-672), so this AABB is arithmetic and not a Godot measurement pass. x = PLINTH_SIZE.x = 5.850, and the pads are exactly as wide as the widest slat so the outermost mark reaches the same +/-2.925 at every variant. y = -0.100 (plinth underside) to 4.340 (rail top) = 4.440; the tallest slat the rack can build tops out at BASE_Y + HALF_T + TRAVEL*1.0 + SLAT_THK/2 = 4.180, 0.060 m clear of the rail's underside, so the rail and not a slat sets the ceiling. Both `mass` and `count` are normalised to reach 1.0 exactly (CEILING is the bay's own max, MAX_PARTS 5185 makes log(5185)/log(5185) = 1), so 4.180 is reached and not merely bounded. z = PLINTH_SIZE.z = 0.560; the deepest tenant is the seam post at -0.270 and the shallowest a relief slat at +0.145. IDENTICAL AT ALL TEN VARIANTS, verified box by box in the Python replica - which is load bearing, see dna.still_note. Re-measure when a Godot pass is run.

dna.default:
ladder=series, reckoning=mass.

BOTH ARE THE CODE'S OWN @export DEFAULTS, read off ladder_hall.gd:403 and :408 and not chosen here. There are no shipped placements to preserve - dna.placements is 0, verified this pass: no map_data.json and no JSON anywhere under commons/ names this token - so the defaults had only to be the strongest single readings.

DIVERGENCE FROM THE FOUR SOURCES, STATED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED OVER. All four benches default to `figure` (fractal_arch_bench.gd:55, sierpinski_bench.gd:55, mandelbrot_bench.gd:46, julia_bench.gd:47 are each `@export var ladder: String = "figure"`). This hall defaults to `series` instead, and the picture says why: at `figure` every bay carries exactly ONE slat, which is the sparsest frame in the sheet (15.11% ink on the crop against `section`'s 42.28%) and is the one value that shows no climb at all. `series` is the whole legality argument for a still - an iteration count laid out sideways is visible, played in time it is not - so opening there opens on the thing the artifact exists to make sayable. The divergence is deliberate and it is the only place this hall does not follow its sources.

reckoning=mass because at `mass` all four bays move at every ladder value, and at `count` bays C and D are flat lines by construction. Opening on count would open on a sheet where half the row does not climb, which is the FINDING and not the introduction to it.

DECLARED ORDER IS ladder THEN reckoning, and it is load bearing. See dna.budget.
dna.was: nothing. This token did not exist before this pass, and neither did the arrangement. Measured, not assumed: a sweep of all 108 registry files returns exactly four entries declaring a `ladder` axis - fractal_arch_bench, sierpinski_bench, mandelbrot_bench and julia_bench, all four in fractals.json - and all four declare [figure, series, seed, relief, section]. No two of these four constructions have ever appeared in one frame, so the question of whether the shared word buys a shared climb could not be put.
dna.note:
WHAT THE FOUR BENCHES ACTUALLY DECLARE, read out of the code for this entry rather than transcribed (LAW 1).

NONE OF THE FOUR USES @export_enum, AND THIS IS THE FIRST CORRECTION. All four spell the axis as a PLAIN typed String with the values in a trailing comment and a const beside it:

  fractal_arch_bench.gd:55   @export var ladder: String = "figure"  # figure | series | seed | relief | section
  sierpinski_bench.gd:55     the same line
  mandelbrot_bench.gd:46     the same line
  julia_bench.gd:47          the same line

with `const LADDERS: PackedStringArray = ["figure", "series", "seed", "relief", "section"]` on the next line of each, and apply_grid_config gating on `LADDERS.has(...)`. So the five values are real and identical character for character in all four files, but they are NOT enforced by the engine's property hint in any of them, and `python tools/check_dna_declarations.py` therefore has only a const to read there, not a hint_string. THIS HALL IS DIFFERENT ON PURPOSE: ladder_hall.gd:403 and :408 are genuine `@export_enum`, and gd:530-583 reads the hint string BACK OUT of get_property_list() and compares it to the const in BOTH directions AND in order, then checks that MEASURE and PARTS carry a rung list for every declared value. That is a stronger gate than any of its four sources has.

WHERE THE FAMILY AGREES. The value list, and the roles: `figure` is the legacy build untouched; `series` is the whole climb tiled in SPACE; `seed` is the first rung at full size; `relief` is every rung as a complete figure on its own z plane; `section` is one figure cut across the ladder PLUS a lit rail on every seam. All four draw a lit MeshInstance3D on `section` and on nothing else, which is why the seam post in this hall exists at that value and at no other.

WHERE IT DISAGREES, and none of it is a detail:

  1. THE RUNG COUNT IS NOT SHARED, and the code's own tables say so: MEASURE/PARTS carry 4, 5, 6 and 6 entries at `series` and `relief`. The arch and the gasket count recursion depths; the two escape-time benches count fractional iteration budgets, maxi(int(round(70*f)),2) for f in [.06,.09,.14,.22,.45,1.0] = [4,6,10,15,32,70].
  2. WHAT A RUNG IS SPLITS THE FAMILY IN HALF. For the arch and the gasket a rung is a recursion DEPTH decided before any geometry exists. For the Mandelbrot and the Julia it is a per-pixel RESULT on a fixed 72x72 = 5184 lattice, so the mesh count is 5184 at 4 iterations and 5184 at 70. That split is the whole reason `reckoning` has two values.
  3. `seed` IS THE CLEANEST DISAGREEMENT. PARTS gives the arch 11 against its figure's 165 and the gasket 3 against 243, while both escape-time bays give 5184 against 5184 - identical to the last bit. The seed of an escape-time test is not a smaller object; it is the same object asked a shorter question. Those two cells are the only exact zeros this hall's own matrix contains, and they are the closest pair (see dna.predicted_degeneracy).
  4. `relief` is the only value at which the escape-time bays' part counts move at all, because _shell emits INTERIORS ONLY: 1900/1450/1174/1042/936/894 for the Mandelbrot against 1394/1160/992/904/686/344 for the Julia.

THE ARITHMETIC THE HEIGHTS COME FROM (gd:642-652), recomputed here: `count` is log(parts+1)/log(5185), ONE shared normaliser across all four bays, so equal heights across bays mean equal part counts and nothing else. `mass` is measure/CEILING[bay], each bay's own maximum, so the four columns are each other's scale-free comparison and equal heights across bays mean NOTHING. Every equality this entry declares is in `count`. Bay-crop coincidences in `mass` are normalisation accidents and must never be reported as equalities.

CORRECTIONS TO THE RECORD (LAW 1: the code wins):

  - THE BRIEF FOR THIS PASS SAYS julia_bench DECLARES ITS LADDER SIX TIMES, WITH `figure` TWICE. IT NO LONGER DOES. Both HEAD and the working tree of commons/artifacts/registry/fractals.json declare five, in family order. Commit c00e666f0 (2026-08-13) removed the duplicate; the brief is stale. Verified by parsing the file and by `git show HEAD:...`. Not this file's business to edit, and nothing to edit.
  - ladder_hall.gd's own header (C6) quotes a rendered subject-width range of "439 to 446 px = 57.8% to 58.7%". That reproduces EXACTLY in the independent replica built for this entry - 439 to 446 px of 760 - as do its bay-move figures of 29.5 px and 48.9 px and its screen-basis coefficients. The geometry in that header is sound.
  - THE ONE NUMBER IN THAT HEADER THAT DOES NOT REPRODUCE is its predicted magnitude of "16.9%" for the closest pair. Under artifact_dna_critic's actual code path the same pair measures 0.2243% frame / 4.4602% focus, and under a true-background probe 3.5486% / 70.8873%. Neither is 16.9%, and no currency tried here produces it (whole-frame uncropped 1.2772/25.5438; unresized full-crop 0.2222/4.4435; per-channel focus 82.66%). What DOES reproduce is the figure the header attributes to the brief and calls the floor: 4.457% against a measured focus of 4.4602%, agreeing to 0.07%. So the header's own gate instruction is a FOCUS instruction, and dna.predicted_degeneracy restates it in both currencies rather than leaving it ambiguous.
  - ladder_hall.gd:200-205 gives bay A's slat SCREEN THICKNESS as 10.70 px and calls it the worst mark. Measured directly off the replica as the vertical run at bay A's own centre column, the mark is 12.07 crop px; the 10.70 is the pure y-component with the top face's 0.160 m depth rake excluded, which recomputes here as 10.63 px. Both readings clear LAW 10's floor, the conservative one by 0.63 px. The header's number is right about the component it names and is not the thing a downsample sees.
dna.kin:
`ladder` IS TAKEN, NOT MINTED, and taken character for character (LAW 14): ["figure", "series", "seed", "relief", "section"], the list all four benches carry, in that order. Verified against fractal_arch_bench.gd:56, sierpinski_bench.gd:56, mandelbrot_bench.gd:47 and julia_bench.gd:48, which are four byte-identical `const LADDERS: PackedStringArray` lines. Nothing was added, nothing was dropped, and no value was renamed. This is the fifth token to carry the word and the first not to draw a fractal with it.

`reckoning` IS ALSO REUSED. grain_block.gd:104 is `@export_enum("none", "mass", "void", "count") var reckoning: String = "none"` - the corpus's only prior use, where `mass` is a register filled with MATTER and `count` the same register filled with PIECES. This hall takes two of those four in grain_block's own order and refuses the other two on the record:

  `none` REFUSED because it draws no register at all. Half of a two-value axis publishing a blank register is the removal_room failure - a value that renders nothing and scores as a fact about the harness.
  `void` REFUSED because it draws what the division REMOVED, and an escape-time test has no such quantity. There is no set of cells the Mandelbrot bench 'took away' at iteration 40; there are cells that had not yet escaped. `void` would be a refusal in three bays out of four rather than a reading, and a bay that stands empty because the word does not apply is honest only when the word applies SOMEWHERE in the row.

WHERE THIS ARTIFACT IS STRONGER THAN ITS SOURCES, and where it is still weaker than selection_garden. Stronger: it is the only member of the `ladder` family whose axis is a real @export_enum, and gd:530-583 reads the engine's own hint string back and compares it to the const in both directions and in order, then cross-checks the MEASURE and PARTS table lengths against the declared value count - so a table that did not cover a value would push_error rather than build an empty bay and photograph as a fact about an array length. Weaker: both sides of that check are INTERNAL. selection_garden preloads its owner file and compares against the source's own const at run time. This hall retypes the five strings. If sierpinski_bench renamed a value tomorrow, ladder_hall would keep declaring the old one and every gate would stay green. The hand check was done instead - all four LADDERS lines opened and compared for this entry, today - and the cheap repair is a preload of one bench plus a third comparison.
dna.declines:
`depth` / `iterations` REFUSED AS AN AXIS, and this is the sharpest refusal in the entry because three of the four sources are iterative and the knob is right there. A rung index is exactly the thing LAW 4 forbids when it is played, and exactly the thing a still CAN show when it is laid out in space - which is what `series` and `relief` already do. Promoting `depth` would put the same information on a second axis where it becomes a rate again.

EVERY RATE AND EVERY ANIMATION REFUSED. Three of the four sources animate: fractal_arch_bench sways at sin(t*0.4)*0.06, sierpinski_bench at sin(t*0.4)*0.05, and julia_bench rebuilds its whole field every frame from a drifting c. ladder_hall.gd contains NO _process, NO timer, NO signal, NO tween and NO clock read - grep returns hits for those tokens at gd:109-115, 131, 386-387 and 493 and ALL OF THEM ARE INSIDE COMMENTS. _ready is ungated (gd:483-489) and builds the finished rack from the two exports in one synchronous pass, and apply_grid_config calls the same _rebuild rather than a plain _build, so a grid path that configures before tree entry cannot stack a second rack on the first.

NO SEED NEEDED, AND NONE IS DECLARED (LAW 5). All four benches call `_rng.randomize()`. This file has no randf, no randi, no randomize and no RandomNumberGenerator at all; every position is arithmetic over the constants in MEASURE, PARTS, CEILING and MAX_PARTS. There is nothing for a seed export to pin.

DRAWING THE FOUR FIGURES REFUSED, AND IT IS THE REAL COST OF THIS ARTIFACT (LAW 12). Priced before the cap was chosen: at `relief` the four benches together instantiate 286 + 363 + 7396 + 5480 = 13525 elements, 4.23x the ~3200 budget. Cutting to fit leaves 1275 per escape-time bay, 212 cells a panel, a grid of 14 against the source's 72, and a cell that projects to 1.6 px - under LAW 10's floor. There is no depth at which drawing the fractals answers anything at this frame width, and a faithful Sierpinski at depth 6 and one at depth 3 would be the same photograph, a grey patch of the right density. What that forecloses is named in qfep_connection and is not argued away.

FULL-HEIGHT DIVIDERS FORECLOSED BY ARITHMETIC, NOT TASTE. Measured daylight between adjacent bay marks is 11.85 crop px at its worst (section/mass, the A|B gap). A divider that READS at LAW 10's 10 px and leaves 10 px either side needs 30 px of the 11.85 available, which forces the pitch past 2.5 m, the row past 8.4 m and the frame past 11.2 m - at which point bay A's slat falls under 8.2 px and LAW 10 breaks instead. The kerbs are 0.140 x 0.260 x 0.240 and top out at y 0.260, which is below the lowest slat any variant builds (bay D, section, mass, rung 5, bottom 0.2992), so they divide the row on the ground and are categorically incapable of standing in front of a mark.

PER-BENCH HUES REFUSED AS A SIXTH SIGNAL. Each bay carries a constant tint read off that bench's palette (BAY_TINT, gd:457) and it is CONSTANT PER BAY IN ALL TEN VARIANTS, so it cancels in every diff. Colouring a bay by its ladder VALUE would hand the eye a difference the benches did not produce.

`emissive` IS NOT AN AXIS. gd:411 is a plain `@export var emissive: bool = true` gating the seam post's glow energy and a 0.12 untinted lift on the slats. It is a lighting gate, it is not declared in dna.axes, and it must not be swept.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS ALL TEN VARIANTS, computed by enumerating every box _build would create at all 5 x 2 combinations. The union is 5.850 x 4.440 x 0.560 centred (0, 2.120, 0) and - checked box by box - EVERY ONE OF THE TEN VARIANTS HAS THAT SAME BOX, because the plinth, the rail and the four pads are present in all of them and set all three extents on their own, the pads being exactly as wide as the widest slat. Diagonal 7.365440, radius 3.682720.

THE RIG: dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing = 3.682720 / 0.3057307 * 1.9 * 0.62 = 14.189756 m, so the visible frame is 2 * PAD * radius * framing = 8.676488 m wide.

WHY 0.62. At framing 1.0 the rig fits by bounding SPHERE and the row would be 41.9% of frame width - the thin-subject case. At 0.62 the union box projects to 446 px of 760 = 58.68% of frame WIDTH, and the rack is 4.440 m tall in an 8.676 m frame, which leaves the margin the key light's specular fringe needs and the replica does not model. Below about 0.55 the daylight and the worst-bay mark both go under their floors together (see dna.still_note R4-equivalent), and above about 0.70 bay A's slat drops under LAW 10.

LAW 7: THE GAUGE IS PER BAY AND THIS ROW IS THE CASE THAT MAKES IT MATTER. The row lies 0.56 aligned with the view axis, so at dist 14.189756 the four bays sit at 15.5795 / 14.6530 / 13.7265 / 12.8000 m - a 1.2172x depth spread - and each has its own pixel scale. One number for the row would be a number for x = 0, a point between bays B and C where this artifact builds nothing. That is the error that cost the last wave a repair and it is not made here.

THE GAUGE THE VERDICT IS COMPUTED ON IS NOT THE FRAME. artifact_dna_critic crops each pair to the UNION of the two subject boxes (:313-334) and only then resizes to 160 x 160 (:93), so framing cancels out of the mark gauge. The crop is 446 x 464 px, giving 0.35874 px per frame-px in x and 0.34483 in y. MEASURED off the replica at that gauge, as a vertical run at each bay's own centre column rather than off a bbox:

  bay              depth m    slat vertical run (crop px)
  A fractal_arch    15.5795         12.07   <- WORST BAY, THE FARTHEST
  B sierpinski      14.6530         12.76
  C mandelbrot      13.7265         13.79
  D julia           12.8000         14.48

The pure thickness component at bay A, with the top face's 0.160 m depth rake excluded, is 10.63 px - still over LAW 10's floor, by 0.63 px. That is thin, and it is why framing is not free to raise.
dna.still_note:
READ THE Z-STACK AND THE BACKGROUND PROBE BEFORE BELIEVING ANY NUMBER OFF THIS SHEET.

LAW 9: NOTHING OPAQUE SITS IN FRONT OF A MARK. Written out as intervals, every layer:
  seam post        z -0.270 .. -0.170   only at `section`, STRICTLY BEHIND every slat
  kerb dividers    z -0.120 .. +0.120   but y <= 0.260, below every slat, and 0.750 m away in x from any bay centre
  plinth and pads  z -0.280 .. +0.280   but y <= 0.180, below every slat
  flat slats       z -0.080+0.002k .. +0.080-0.002k
  relief slat 0    z -0.155 .. +0.005    relief slat 5  z +0.005 .. +0.145
  datum rail       z -0.050 .. +0.050   at y 4.240..4.340, over a v=1 slat's 4.180 top
NO GLASS, NO BEZEL, NO CASE, NO FRAME. operations_gallery built its bezel as one solid 24 mm slab enclosing the panel face and every mark its axis drew; four values were four photographs of one slab and every gate was green.

THE ONE PLACE A MARK COULD OCCLUDE ANOTHER IS `relief`, AND IT IS NESTED SO IT CANNOT. Screen-x shift per z step is 0.581035 * 0.030 = 0.017431 m; the screen-x half-width shrinks 0.813878 * 0.035 + 0.581035 * 0.002 = 0.029648 m per step. 0.017431 < 0.029648, so every nearer slat sits strictly INSIDE the previous one's screen-x span. Relief here is carried by the nested TAPER (slat 5 is 0.550 m against slat 0's 0.900), not by the rake, and that is the sources' own behaviour: all four benches build relief as nested plates whose z step measures under 1 px after the downsample. Slats also nest in all three axes (length -0.012k, thickness -0.002k, depth -0.004k) so no two ever share a face plane; coplanar faces are z-fighting speckle, i.e. a NON-DETERMINISTIC still, which cost pressure_yard a pass.

LAW 8: DAYLIGHT, MEASURED PER BAY THROUGH THE PERSPECTIVE CAMERA AT THE WIDEST VARIANT OF BOTH AXES. The furniture is continuous across the row by design, so a silhouette read off the PNG cannot see this gap - the MARKS are what must not touch, and every slat and post corner was projected to find it. The tightest gap is always A|B, the farthest pair, and its minimum over all ten variants is 33.03 px at 760 = 11.85 px on the critic's crop, at section/mass. The widest tenant is a MARK and not the furniture: relief slat 0 reaches 0.456306 m of screen-x from its bay centre against the pad's 0.424349 m, which is why the pad was cut to 0.900 x 0.200. RELIEF_DZ is the constant most at risk - raising it from 0.030 to 0.060 puts the tenant at 0.474 m and forces the pitch past 1.72.

LAW 11: THE SUBJECT IS AIRY, NOT SMALL. The union box is 446 px of 760 = 58.68% of frame WIDTH, and within that crop the ink swings from 15.11% (figure/mass) to 42.28% (section/mass); measured the critic's way over the whole 160 x 160 frame, subject_fraction runs 6.42% to 17.55%, far above BLANK_SUBJECT 0.002, so there is no NO RENDER risk. A row of four separated bays leaves most of its bounding volume empty BY CONSTRUCTION - the empty travel above and below every slat IS the measuring scale - so that swing is the axis working. Do not tighten dna.framing on it.

THE ONE THING THAT COULD MAKE THIS SHEET LIE, AND IT IS NOT THE ARTIFACT. artifact_dna_critic neutralises each crop against pixel (3,3) OF THE CROP, on the docstring's assumption that a corner is background by construction. IT IS NOT BACKGROUND HERE. The subject bbox is (184, 170, 630, 634): its left edge comes from the plinth's bottom-left corner at row ~508, and its top edge from the DATUM RAIL, whose top-left corner projects to (186.8, 170.3). The probe at crop (3,3) = frame (187, 173) therefore lands on the rail's first lit column, one pixel inside its silhouette, and the neutralisation subtracts L = 107.55 instead of L = 1.0. What that does is fold the image about mid-grey: the true background maps to 106.55 and bay A's stone slat (L 212.3) maps to 104.75, so THE HALL'S FARTHEST BAY ENDS UP 1.8 GREY LEVELS FROM THE GROUND IT STANDS ON and nearly vanishes from the measurement while remaining plainly visible in the picture. Measured consequence on the closest pair: bay A's own crop reads 0.2869% where bay B's reads 7.5344%, a 26x split between two bays whose marks move 29.4 px and 48.9 px. This is a property of the instrument meeting a full-width rail, not a fault in the rack, and it is ONE PIXEL from flipping - if the real bbox opens one column further left the probe lands on background and every number in the sheet rises about 15x. dna.predicted_degeneracy therefore pre-registers BOTH branches and gates on the lower.

dna.budget:
5 x 2 = 10 variants against build_dna_gallery's default cap of 16 (tools/build_dna_gallery.py:136), so AT THE DEFAULT NOTHING IS TRIMMED and the coverage record is complete. The dot_aligner fault - a four-value axis rendered at two and judged as four - cannot occur at this size.

DECLARED ORDER IS ladder THEN reckoning AND IT DECIDES WHAT BREAKS AT A LOWERED CAP. build_dna_gallery trims values from the END of the LATER axis until the running cross product fits, and an axis left with fewer than 2 values is DROPPED WHOLE rather than shortened (:78-96). With `ladder` first, at cap 9: ladder keeps all five (5 <= 9), then reckoning is trimmed from 2 to 1, which is under 2, so `reckoning` VANISHES and the sheet becomes a single-axis sweep with the channel silently pinned at mass. With `reckoning` first, cap 9 would instead render 2 x 4 = 8 and drop `section` - the value that carries the seam post, the one thing all four benches agree on, and the loudest pair in the sheet at 3.4250% frame. Both sacrifices are bad; the ruling is the cap, not the order. DO NOT RUN THIS SWEEP BELOW --max=10.

NO GODOT RENDER EXISTS YET, and no verdict about this artifact - alive or dead - should be issued until the sweep has run. Every number in this block is Python: the geometry, the projection, the stage and the critic's metric, all re-implemented, and the artifact has never been compiled or booted from this entry. Order of operations: `python tools/check_dna_declarations.py` first (it will read the real @export_enum hint strings, which this hall has and its four sources do not), then a headless compile check, then the sweep, then the critic.

TWO GDSCRIPT FORMS THE ORCHESTRATOR SHOULD WATCH ON THE COMPILE PASS, because if either fails the whole artifact is down and nothing in this entry means anything. gd:413-414 declare `const LADDERS: PackedStringArray = [...]` and `const RECKONINGS: PackedStringArray = [...]` - an array LITERAL against a packed-array hint, which is a constant expression and has shipped precedent in all four bench files, so it is expected to parse; a CONSTRUCTOR call there would not. And gd:624-627 use `var length: float = ...`, `var z: float = ...` with explicit types rather than `:=` inference, which is the form that survives; the header's own MEASURE and PARTS are `Array` and not typed arrays, so no inference is needed there either.

THE STANDPOINT CAVEAT APPLIES IN ADVANCE. This rack is read against HEIGHT, close to a frontal reading, and the sweep's standpoint is 36 degrees off frontal. If any pair comes back flat, run `python tools/probe_anamorphic.py --token=ladder_hall --axis=<axis>` before believing it - five of seven dead verdicts in this corpus were false. This one has an additional false-flat trap of its own: six cells are SUPPOSED to be 0.000%, and a bay mean that sags on them is the design, not a fault.

AND THE THING MOST LIKELY TO BE WRONG IN THIS ENTRY, named so it is not discovered as a surprise: the background-probe branch (dna.still_note). Which of 0.2243% and 3.5486% the sweep lands on turns on ONE PIXEL of the subject bbox, and the replica has no antialiasing, so its bbox edge is harder than the real one's. If the measured sheet comes back roughly 15x this table across the board, that is the other branch and it is healthy. If it comes back roughly 15x on some pairs and not others, the bbox is moving between variants and the crops are not congruent - which would be a real fault and would need the union pre-pass checked.
dna.measured: MEASURED 2026-08-13, first capture. 10 variants, rejected=0, so every swept value is known to have arrived. Peak 13.416% of frame, subject 15.586%, BITES, and verify_batch reports every axis separating by at least 1.0%. No exact zeros anywhere. THE PREDICTION NAMED THE PAIR AND THE RUNNER-UP, which is the strongest form this gate has produced. predicted_degeneracy called the closest pair ladder=figure vs ladder=seed at reckoning=count - NOT an adjacent pair in declared order - at 0.2243% frame. Measured: that exact pair at 1.66%, 7.4x above the floor. It also called series vs relief at count as the second-quietest; measured second-quietest is that exact pair at 2.423%. Two independent orderings, both correct, from a Python rasteriser that had never booted the artifact. AND THE ADVERSARIAL CRITIC IS RIGHT ABOUT WHAT IT COSTS. Builder and critic derived the resolvable value step independently and agree to four decimals - dv = SLAT_THK / TRAVEL = 0.400/3.600 = 0.1108, an invariant of the geometry that framing cannot move, because tightening the camera scales the bar and the gap together. The header declared it in advance as 'about nine distinguishable levels'. The critic enumerated what that actually eats: of 136 declared rungs, 81 survive as visible bars; 21 of the 55 losses are honest (identical source values, correctly one bar) and 34 are DISTINCT MEASUREMENTS FUSED INTO A NEIGHBOUR. THE CASUALTIES INCLUDE THE HEADLINE. sierpinski's exact (3/4)^d at d = 3, 4, 5 - 0.620031, 0.465023, 0.348767, the fact this hall is proudest of - photographs as ONE BAR at series/mass and relief/mass. So does bay A's count column, 33 / 77 / 165, the only bay whose count is supposed to climb, which reads as two bars. Visible in the sheet without any tool: at series/mass and relief/mass, bays C and D are solid blocks where the design intends a ladder. SO IT WORKS AS AN AXIS AND FAILS AS AN INSTRUMENT, and that is the honest verdict rather than a compromise. The ten variants are distinct and well separated; a reader recovers an ORDER OF MAGNITUDE from any bay and never a part count. The two laws are in direct conflict here and no tuning resolves them: separating bay C's tightest pair (0.226466 vs 0.201003, and 0.180556 vs 0.172454) needs SLAT_THK under 0.029 m, which is about 2.4 px and far under the 10 px floor a mark must clear to measure at all. The fix is a LOG mapping or per-bay normalisation - a design change, not a tune - and it is not made here. KEPT rather than held, because the number is real, the prediction held twice, and the limitation is now measured and named instead of being discovered later from a flat pair.
